key_insight: Under tight evaluation budgets, enriching CMA-ES with differential-evolution trial vectors improves optimization, but solver choice still depends on problem structure and stopping time.
engineering_relevance: Budget-aware hybrid optimizers can improve expensive parametric architectural and structural design searches within practical wall-clock limits.
method: Inject differential-evolution trial vectors into CMA-ES sampling.
Combine particle swarm optimization with success-history adaptation, differential-evolution injection and local refinement.
Delay population-size reduction in adaptive differential evolution to suit small evaluation budgets.
evidence_signal: With all evaluations counted under a 1,200-evaluation cap, the CMA-ES hybrid ranked first across seven shifted and rotated benchmarks at 10 and 30 variables; in a 15-minute, 85-variable shell-design test, it and plain CMA-ES achieved final objective values 48% below the best external tool.
watch_item: Do not assume a universal winner: differential evolution led on the mixed-binary building problem, and local refinement helped only when its result re-entered the population.
paper_title: Hybrid metaheuristics for architectural design optimization under small evaluation and wall-clock budgets
